purpose: Test on a third independent time sample whether the already replicated broadband/scale-like H10S2-over-H10N1 10-80 Hz baseline-power offset is temporally persistent rather than driven by a small number of isolated windows.

new_window_contract.independence_from_prior_samples: The new windows begin at 06:00 UTC and do not overlap either the prior 00:00 spectral-shape sample or the prior 12:00 asymmetry-replication sample.

frequency_contract.selection_basis: Exactly the same frozen broadband interval used by the prior replication and morphology gates.

per_complete_window: raw S2-minus-N1 10-80 Hz integrated-power ratio in dB
response-corrected S2-minus-N1 10-80 Hz integrated-power ratio in dB
aggregate: fraction of complete windows with raw ratio >= 6 dB
fraction of complete windows with corrected ratio >= 6 dB
fraction of complete windows with both raw and corrected ratios >= 6 dB

classification_thresholds.engineering_interpretation: A temporally stable scale offset requires a large median effect, an interquartile range no wider than 3 dB, and at least 80% of complete paired windows independently exceeding the 6 dB floor in both raw and corrected power. These thresholds classify persistence only; they do not identify cause.

claim_ceiling: A TEMPORALLY_STABLE result establishes only that a large broadband H10S2-over-H10N1 baseline-power offset persists across this third frozen time sample with limited dispersion. It narrows the morphology away from a single isolated episode but does not distinguish persistent environmental/site noise from deployment, calibration, gain, or other station-path mechanisms. A VARIABLE result likewise does not erase the two previous independent findings. Neither outcome validates 119 Hz or increases target evidence.
